1: Once more I shall teach you the supreme knowledge, the highest of all knowledge. Knowing it, all the sages have gone from here to supreme perfection.
2: Those who rely on this knowledge come to share my own nature. They are not born even at creation, and at dissolution they are not disturbed.
3: The great brahman is my womb, and in it I place the embryo. From that, descendant of Bharata, all beings come into being.
4: Whatever forms come into being in any womb, son of Kuntī, the great brahman is their womb, and I am the father who gives the seed.
5: Sattva, rajas and tamas: these are the guṇas, born of nature. Mighty-armed one, they bind the imperishable embodied one in the body.
6: Of these, sattva is stainless, and so it gives light and is free from ill. It binds, sinless one, by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge.
7: Know that rajas has the nature of passion and arises from thirst and attachment. It binds the embodied one, son of Kuntī, by attachment to action.
8: But know that tamas is born of ignorance and deludes all embodied ones. It binds, descendant of Bharata, by heedlessness, laziness and sleep.
9: Sattva attaches one to happiness and rajas to action, descendant of Bharata. But tamas veils knowledge and attaches one to heedlessness.
10: Sattva arises, descendant of Bharata, by overpowering rajas and tamas. Rajas arises by overpowering sattva and tamas, and tamas likewise by overpowering sattva and rajas.
11: When light, which is knowledge, is born at all the gates of this body, then one should know that sattva has increased.
12: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and longing: these are born, bull of the Bharatas, when rajas has increased.
13: Absence of light, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion: these are born, joy of the Kurus, when tamas has increased.
14: But when an embodied being dies while sattva is strong, that being reaches the stainless worlds of those who know the highest.
15: One who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. Likewise, one who dies in tamas is born in the wombs of the deluded.
16: They say that the fruit of action well done is stainless and of the nature of sattva. But the fruit of rajas is sorrow, and the fruit of tamas is ignorance.
17: From sattva knowledge is born, and from rajas greed. From tamas come heedlessness and delusion, and ignorance too.
18: Those who stand in sattva go upward. Those of rajas stay in the middle. Those of tamas, standing in the workings of the lowest guṇa, go downward.
19: When the seer sees that there is no doer other than the guṇas, and knows what is higher than the guṇas, that seer reaches my state of being.
20: Going beyond these three guṇas, which arise from the body, the embodied one is freed from the sorrows of birth, death and old age, and attains the deathless.
21: Lord, by what marks is one known to have gone beyond these three guṇas? How does such a person behave, and how does one pass beyond these three guṇas?
22: Son of Pāṇḍu, such a person does not hate light, activity or delusion when they have come, and does not long for them when they have gone.
23: Such a person sits like one unconcerned and is not shaken by the guṇas. Thinking that it is the guṇas that act, such a person stands firm and does not waver.
24: Such a person is the same in sorrow and in happiness, abides within, and is steady. To such a person a clod, a stone and gold are the same, the dear and the not dear are equal, and blame and praise of oneself are equal.
25: Such a person is equal in honour and dishonour, equal toward the side of friend and the side of enemy, and gives up all undertakings. That person is said to have gone beyond the guṇas.
26: And one who serves me with the unswerving yoga of devotion goes fully beyond these guṇas and is fit to become brahman.
27: For I am the foundation of brahman, of the deathless and the imperishable, of the everlasting dharma and of absolute happiness.
